newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong continues record surge, Dow lifts Tokyo.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong continues record surge, Dow lifts Tokyo.

text.p: Blue-chips, banks and a raging Dow industrials buoyed some Asian markets on Tuesday, pushing Hong Kong's bourse to another record close and supporting the markets in Tokyo and Singapore.
Other Asian markets were generally mixed, with economic woes weighing down the Seoul bourse, and profit-takers cashing in in Taiwan. The Thai bourse ended down one percent on political uncertainty.
Tokyo stocks ended higher, supported by a booming New York stock market and towed by blue-chip issues, brokers said.
They also said market participants were eager to see the Bank of Japan's (BOJ) "tankan" business sentiment survey to be released on Wednesday.
At the end of the session, the Nikkei 225 was up 124.68 points or 0.59 percent at 21,418.25.
"International issues which are seen doing well stole the limelight once again today as investors eagerly snapped up the shares," said Nomura Securities strategist Masaaki Higashida.
Brokers said Wall Street's overnight surge aided the Tokyo market psychologically. The Dow rose 76 points or 1.17 percent to about 6,548, the biggest point rise since August 2.
In Hong Kong, the Hang Seng Index charged to a record close, propelled amid heavy volume by a surge in banking shares and a continued bullish tone in the property sector.
The index rose 245.94 points or 1.86 percent to close at 13,485.33 after hitting an intraday record high at 13,495.38.
"HongKong Bank and Hang Seng are leading the market," said Geoff Galbraith, institutional sales trader at Nava SC Securities. "They contribute half of the index gain."
Brisk buying of selected blue-chips, namely banking stocks, and small capitalised stocks boosted the Singapore stock market to a firmer close, dealers said.
They said interest was evident mainly from overseas fund managers who were adjusting their portfolio of regional stocks.
The key Straits Times Industrials Index ended 14.19 points up at 2,219.88. Total turnover was a healthy 196.49 million shares, with gainers leading losers by 201 to 167.
New Zealand shares closed strongly with demand spread among the leaders and strong support among some second-tier issues.
The NZSE-40 Capital Index ended 17.13 points or 0.73 percent higher at 2,356.29.
Brokers said Wall Street's record close may have been behind the solid demand for the leading issues.
Thai shares ended down one percent at 958.14 amid political uncertainty over the shape of the new cabinet being formed by Prime Minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh, brokers said.
Seoul stocks slid further to close at a new 37-month low despite the government's plan to boost share buying by investment trusts, brokers said.
"The government plan helped boost the market. But fears of worsening fundamentals were more dominant," said Kim Wan-hee, a broker at Dongsuh Securities.
The stock index closed 0.48 of a point or 0.07 percent lower at a provisional 715.97, the lowest since October 9, 1993 when it ended at 712.35.
Manila stocks finished down amidst thin trading, pulled down by selling in blue chips, traders said. The main index closed 30.18 points lower, or 0.97 percent, at 3,074.28 points.

Taiwan share prices finished slightly lower as profit-takers cashed in on the market's dramatic November rise of more than 300 points. The weighted index finished 11.10 points or a scant 0.16 percent lower at 6,927.77.
Australian shares closed weaker as sellers, worried about the effect of the stronger Australian dollar on the resource sector, took control of the market.
The All Ordinaries index ended 12.7 points or 0.53 percent weaker at 2,382, after hitting a life-high of 2408.9 early on.
Brent crude futures pared earlier losses in late trading as bearish sentiment from Monday continued, brokers said.
January Brent crude futures were last traded on SIMEX at $22.60 per barrel, down two cents from London's settlement on Monday but 10 cents above the SIMEX intraday low.

The dollar eased slightly on the yen on profit-taking in late trade after rising briefly earlier on concerns over Japan's financial system. Dealers were awaiting the release of the Bank of Japan's quarterly corporate survey due early on Wednesday.
At 1000 GMT the dollar traded at 112.40/45 yen and 1.5231/36 marks.
